messages:
maya: Heads-up — OrsonHealth cutover is scheduled for tomorrow 09:00 PST. Quick sync: they ran into two blockers in staging that could affect the live cutover: networking route leak and KMS key rotation errors. Also noted gaps in audit log retention that might surface during their security review. Flagging as near-term renewal-risk until we confirm mitigation plan.

devon: I dug into their VPC config — route table on the private subnet doesn't advertise 10.1.0.0/16 to our peering attachment. Healthchecks are failing because the health-prober IPs are not allowed in their FW. I'll send a minimal fw snippet they can drop in.

sam: I'll take ownership of the infra changes on our side. Plan: (1) provision temporary egress rule to allow prod healthchecks (2) create a service role to assume their KMS key for the runtime (3) open a support ticket for key rotation rollback if needed. Need the customer KMS ARN and the account-id for the trust policy.

nora: Security POV — KMS rotation must not invalidate existing session tokens; ensure we perform a staged rotation and test re-encrypt/decrypt. Also request audit-logs retention >= 90 days for their compliance team. I'll attach a short checklist of evidence they need to upload.

maya: Copying what I'll send to them now (short hand):

maya: Firewall allowlist snippet (ask them to apply to their private subnet):
```
# allow healthcheck IPs from redwood (replace with actual list)
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -s 54.23.12.34 --dport 8080 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -s 54.23.12.35 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
# if using cloud firewall, add inbound rules for 54.23.12.34/32 and 54.23.12.35/32 on tcp:8080,443
```

maya: IAM assume-role template for their KMS delegation: 
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDDED_ACCOUNT_ID:role/redwood-runtime"},
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"
    }
  ]
}
```

maya: Minimal KMS key policy we recommend (rotate plan must include alias switch and staged rekey):
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Sid": "Allow use from redwood runtime","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::REDDED_ACCOUNT_ID:role/redwood-runtime"},"Action":["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey*"],"Resource":"*"}
  ]
}
```

infra-bot: Runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood.com/priv-deploys/cutover-checklist — includes preflight, rollback, and telemetry verification steps.

devon: Owner/ETA matrix:
- devon: network guidance -> sending fw + route snippet to customer by EOD today
- sam: infra changes & support ticket -> will have temp egress and role by 03:00 UTC tomorrow
- nora: security checklist & evidence request -> posting to their workspace and product portal in 1h

maya: I've also captured their feedback from staging call: they want clearer SSO instructions (OIDC vs SAML differences) and an explicit example of the KMS alias swap. They said longer audit retention (180d) would be preferred if feasible.

sam: Support ticket created: #CS-84219. If rotation rollback is needed we escalate to oncall runtime team with that ticket reference. I've attached minimal logs from the failed key usage.

nora: If they request 180d retention, we need a quick ROI/price call-out. That might be a commercial ask — flagging for AMs. Also require encrypted delivery of their audit artifacts (S3 presigned link or secure upload).

devon: I'll include a one-pager with the KMS alias swap example + quick rollback steps. That should reduce friction.

maya: Outcome & next steps:
- we confirm KMS ARN + account id from customer by 17:00 PT today
- devon to push fw & route snippets, sam to stage infra changes pre-cutover
- nora to collect evidence checklist and retention ask for AMs

maya: Renewal-risk note: currently medium because customer had a failed staging deploy. If we hit the mitigations above within the next 48h and provide the runbook + evidence, risk should drop to low.

maya: tagging @devon @sam @nora — please update this thread when your step is done. :thumbsup:
